explain.text: `credit_concentration_risk_hhi` (Credit Concentration Risk HHI) measures how concentrated a credit portfolio is using the Herfindahl-Hirschman index. You pass `exposures`, the per-name exposure amounts, which must be non-negative with at least one positive. It turns each into a share of total exposure and sums the squared shares. A value of 1 means a single-name portfolio, while 1/n means n names with perfectly even exposure. The inverse, 1/HHI, gives the effective number of independent exposures, also called the diversification score.

when.text:
`credit_concentration_risk_hhi` (Credit Concentration Risk HHI) fits when you want a single number showing how concentrated a credit portfolio is across names.

- You have per-name exposure amounts (`exposures`) and want to see whether a few borrowers dominate the portfolio.
- You want a diversification score, since `1/HHI` gives the effective number of independent exposures.
- You want to compare portfolios, or track one over time, against clear reference points: an HHI of 1 means a single-name portfolio, and 1/n means perfectly granular.
- You only have exposure sizes, with no need for default probabilities, correlations or loss estimates.
